append.detail: Built 2026-11-16: lib/hunts/graph/branches.ts and lib/hunts/mystery.ts. Exclusive choice: missions sharing a choice_group are one choice; evaluate counts the earliest accepted credit in the group, closes the other members and ignores any later credit for them, so a choice cannot be changed while its credit stands (a staff reversal of that credit reopens it, by design, so a voided claim cannot strand a player). Alternative path: missions sharing a fallback_group are one objective; one credit satisfies every rule that names any member, under one bucket, and the rest close. validateGraph enumerates the choice paths (at most 64, CHOICE_LIMIT beyond) and refuses any reachable set of choices that cannot finish (BRANCH_DEAD_END), a malformed group (BRANCH_INVALID), and a Mystery on the route to the finish that has no fallback (MYSTERY_NO_FALLBACK); chapters are checked per path too. Mystery: a mission of kind answer is claimed through the existing door (scan, then claimAsPlayer with an answer). The answer is stored only as a salted scrypt hash in hunt_missions.answer_hash, compared in constant time, and selected by no player read; a run gets 5 judged guesses, the fallback hint from the second wrong one, then a lockout that leaves the fallback mission as the way on. The choice race: no new command. Both branches go through hunt_claim_apply, whose progress-count check under the run lock (FH-049T) answers the second one stale_progress; claimAsPlayer then rereads, evaluate closes the branch, and it is refused. No migration. What the database enforces: the count check under the run lock, one progress row per run and mission, and one hunt_claims row per run, mission and evidence id, which is what bounds the answer attempts (answer:1 to answer:5). What it does not: it has no rule that two members of a choice group cannot both hold progress, so a credit written outside claimAsPlayer (a staff approval of a held claim) can add a second row; the evaluator then keeps the earlier one and ignores the later. Tested here against a fake database that copies the count check and the unique key, not against Postgres; the SQL is covered by the existing pgTAP files, which this change does not touch. Not built here, moved to FH-042S: the player answer form and wording, the authoring fields, and a player view of a locked-out Mystery.
